Add a second absorption path for double-absorption models

Source: R/addSecondAbsorption.R
addSecondAbsorption.Rd

Adds a parallel absorption path (depot2) to a model that already has first-order absorption through depot, for Monolix-style double-absorption models: one dose record is split at translation time into two parallel inputs with a logit-parameterized F1 apportionment. The second path can itself be zero-order (type = "zero", a modeled dur(depot2) input), first-order (type = "first", ka2), or a transit chain (delay = "transit"), with an optional lag.

Usage

addSecondAbsorption(
  ui,
  type = c("first", "zero"),
  delay = c("none", "lag", "transit"),
  n = NULL,
  central = "central",
  depot = "depot",
  depot2 = "depot2",
  ka = "ka",
  ka2 = "ka2",
  tk0 = "tk0",
  f1 = 0.7
)

Arguments

ui

The model as a function (or something convertible to an rxUi object)

type

second-path input type: "zero" for a zero-order (modeled-duration) input or "first" for a first-order (ka2) input

delay

second-path delay: "none", "lag" (an alag on the second path), or "transit" (a transit chain feeding the second path)

n

number of transit compartments when delay = "transit"

central

central compartment name

depot

depot compartment name

depot2

name of the second depot compartment

ka

absorption rate parameter name

ka2

name of the second first-order absorption rate

tk0

name of the zero-order duration on the second path

f1

initial fraction of the dose entering the first path, in (0,1)

Value

a model with two parallel absorption paths

Details

Only one second absorption path is supported per model; applying this twice raises an error.

See also

Other Absorption building blocks: addDepot(), addTransit(), addWeibullAbs(), addZeroOrderAbs(), convertAbsForceLongerDelay(), convertAbsSequential(), convertTransitMtt(), removeDepot(), removeTransit(), removeZeroOrderAbs()

Author

Matthew L. Fidler

Examples

pk1cmtDes <- function() {
  ini({
    lka <- 0.45; label("Absorption rate (Ka)")
    lcl <- 1; label("Clearance (CL)")
    lvc <- 3.45; label("Central volume of distribution (V)")
    propSd <- 0.5; label("Proportional residual error (fraction)")
  })
  model({
    ka <- exp(lka)
    cl <- exp(lcl)
    vc <- exp(lvc)
    kel <- cl / vc
    d/dt(depot) <- -ka * depot
    d/dt(central) <- ka * depot - kel * central
    Cc <- central / vc
    Cc ~ prop(propSd)
  })
}


# simultaneous zero-order + first-order (Monolix double absorption)
pk1cmtDes |>
  addSecondAbsorption(type = "first", delay = "lag", f1 = 0.7)
